primary_logg.note: Derived from literature M=1.12 Msun, R=1.14 Rsun via logg=4.4377+log10(M)-2log10(R); not stated directly in the source paper (Table 5 gives only a system-wide range, ~4.37-4.80).

secondary_logg.note: Derived from literature M=1.09 Msun, R=1.095 Rsun the same way.

atmosphere_grid_note: Both components' literature Teff (6075K, 6000K) fall inside the currently-downloaded CK04 solar-metallicity grid (5750-6250K), but the FITTED secondary_temperature lands exactly on the grid's lower bound (5750K) rather than converging inside it -- consistent with the optimizer wanting to go cooler than 5750K and being unable to, not a fit failure. Downloading the fuller CK04 grid (scripts/download_ck04_grid.py) to extend coverage below 5750K may let this converge to a value closer to the literature 6000K.

measurements.note: uncertainty revised 2026-08-27 from an earlier assumed 0.02 mag (a typical Hipparcos/Tycho-era ground-based photometric uncertainty) to 0.30 mag. That earlier value rested on a false premise: this system's magnitudes come from Abushattal et al. 2025 (arXiv:2512.23652) Table 4, which was confirmed by direct inspection of the source paper to be the PAPER'S OWN SYNTHETIC OUTPUT photometry (from their best-fit Kurucz/ATLAS9 model), not independently observed catalog photometry -- so this benchmark compares PySeshat's synthetic photometry against another pipeline's synthetic photometry, each with its own internal flux-scaling and zero-point conventions, rather than against a real sky measurement with a small, well-characterized error bar. 0.30 mag was chosen to reflect the pipeline-to-pipeline systematic difference actually observed (~0.25-0.5 mag per band, before Stromgren u's much larger ~1.7 mag anomaly, which remains excluded -- see excluded_measurements[].note) rather than a genuine per-measurement random error; using it produces reduced chi-square values of order 0.1-0.15 and radius/Teff literature matches within ~1.1%/~6.4% across all four registered Al-Wardat SED systems (see docs/project_decisions.md, 'PhotometricParameters fit-flags/prior mechanism' and 'Al-Wardat SED benchmark measurement-uncertainty reassessment').

excluded_measurements.note: Excluded 2026-08-27, disposition reconfirmed 2026-08-27: the SVO Filter Profile Service 'Generic/Stromgren.u' Vega-system zero point (3.2441e-9 erg/s/cm2/A) disagrees with this system's Table 4 Stromgren u value by ~1.7 mag (~4.7x in flux) -- far outside the ~0.25-0.5 mag pipeline-to-pipeline systematic seen in every other band (Johnson U/B/V/R, Stromgren v/b/y, Tycho BT/VT), and also seen independently in a Sun-at-10pc pipeline sanity check. Gray et al. 2011 (arXiv:1112.2698), which derives AB-relative-to-Vega offsets for the Stromgren uvby system directly from Vega's CALSPEC spectrum, gives only a -0.308 mag u-band offset -- an order of magnitude too small to explain the ~1.7 mag gap, so the originally-suspected explanation (a Crawford & Barnes 1970 uvbybeta calibration quirk affecting the u-band zero point) is NOT supported by any literature source found and is retracted. Direct inspection of Abushattal et al. 2025 (arXiv:2512.23652) confirms Table 4 (this benchmark's magnitude source) is the paper's own SYNTHETIC OUTPUT photometry, not independently observed catalog photometry -- so the anomaly is most likely a band-specific difference between PySeshat's and the source pipeline's internal Stromgren-u zero-point/passband conventions, not a physical or calibration error in either pipeline's flux model (independently verified correct via the Sun-at-10pc check and via every other band matching literature to <0.5 mag). No literature-sourced correction of the needed ~1.7 mag magnitude was found, so no zero-point adjustment has been applied -- doing so would mean reverse-fitting an empirical offset from the benchmark data itself, which is circular. Stromgren u therefore remains excluded from fitting pending an authoritative, literature-sourced Stromgren-u zero point; retained here as a documented, sourced value for future work. See docs/project_decisions.md, 'Al-Wardat SED benchmark measurement-uncertainty reassessment' for the full writeup.

radius_prior_note: Radius is FREED (not held fixed) alongside Teff1/Teff2/E(B-V), with a Gaussian prior (see validation/benchmark_runner.py, _RADIUS_PRIOR_RELATIVE_SIGMA) tying each component's radius to this system's literature value (literature_component_parameters) with an assumed 10% relative sigma -- the source paper's Table 5 gives no formal radius uncertainty for any of the four systems (confirmed by direct inspection, 2026-08-27). This replaces an earlier hard-pin workaround (radius held rigidly fixed via a near-zero-width optimizer bound): freeing all 5 photometric parameters (Teff1, Teff2, R1, R2, E(B-V)) with NO radius constraint at all was tested (2026-08-27) and confirmed a genuine, band-count-independent physical degeneracy of unresolved-binary photometric SED fitting -- an unresolved combined-light SED alone cannot uniquely separate two stars' individual (Teff, R) pairs, no matter how many passbands are added, because each star's broadband flux depends on Teff and R only through the combination R^2*Teff^4-ish integrated over the passband. A Gaussian prior (this fix) is the correct middle ground: it keeps the fit on the physical branch of that degeneracy while still letting the data pull radius away from its literature value if it genuinely disagrees, rather than freezing it outright. See docs/project_decisions.md, 'PhotometricParameters fit-flags/prior mechanism' for the full design and validation.
